title: Give every animation a purpose
principle: Emil Kowalski’s Great Animations / You Don’t Need Animations thesis: motion must earn its place—explain a feature, signal state change, keep spatial consistency, or (rarely) delight on low-frequency surfaces. Frequency of use, perception of speed (ease-out, usually under 300ms), transform+opacity performance, interruptibility, and prefers-reduced-motion decide whether motion helps or burns trust.
procedure: Write the purpose in one sentence before coding motion (explain / state-change / spatial continuity / rare delight).
Estimate frequency: daily-driver controls and keyboard actions default to no animation.
Prefer ease-out and durations under ~300ms for UI; reserve slower/elegant easing for cohesive low-frequency moments (e.g. Sonner-like toast personality).
Animate transform and opacity only; prefer CSS transitions (interruptible) over one-shot keyframes for dynamic UI.
Add prefers-reduced-motion fallback; review the next day with fresh eyes or a critic screenshot.
examplePrompts:
Review every animation in this UI against Emil Kowalski’s purposeful-motion bar:
For each motion, answer: purpose? frequency? duration/easing? transform+opacity only? interruptible? reduced-motion?
Delete any motion that fails purpose or fires on high-frequency/keyboard paths.
Keep total UI transitions ≤300ms with ease-out unless you justify a cohesive exception.
Return a kill-list + kept motions with one-line purposes.

Add enter/exit to this toast. Requirements: spatial consistency (same direction in and out), CSS transition not keyframe, ease that matches the component personality, prefers-reduced-motion → opacity only. Explain purpose in one line.
promptWhy: Checklist forces delete-first review instead of ‘make it smoother’ which usually adds lag.
Toast brief encodes Sonner-style principles (spatial continuity, transitions, personality) without copying proprietary code.
tips: Faster spinner can feel like harder work even when load time is identical—perception matters.
Tooltip pattern: delay first open; subsequent sibling tooltips open with no delay/animation.
Never animate keyboard-initiated actions repeated hundreds of times a day (Raycast example).

workedExamples.title: Marketing explain vs daily chrome
workedExamples.before: Same 400ms ease-in fade on marketing hero and on every command-palette keystroke.
workedExamples.after: Keep purposeful explain-motion on marketing; strip palette/keyboard motion entirely; UI chrome ≤300ms ease-out.
workedExamples.body: Emil: purpose + frequency first. Linear marketing animation that teaches a feature can justify motion; Raycast-like daily tools should not animate open. Cite public essays on emilkowal.ski.

workedExamples.title: Toast spatial consistency
workedExamples.body: Sonner-style enter/exit from the same direction makes swipe-to-dismiss intuitive. Purpose is continuity, not decoration. Prefer transitions so rapid toasts interrupt cleanly.

workedExamples.title: Performance trap
workedExamples.body: Animating layout properties or main-thread springs while the page loads drops frames. Stick to transform/opacity; hardware-accelerated CSS/WAAPI when the main thread is busy (Emil’s Vercel tab example paraphrased).

antiPatterns: ease-in dropdowns that feel sluggish at the moment of response.
Keyframes on rapidly retargeted UI (toasts, toggles) that restart from zero.
checklist: Every kept animation has a written purpose.
High-frequency and keyboard paths are animation-free.

provenance.statement: Design Catalog editorial synthesis of the cited public sources; contracts and decision paths are our implementation guidance, not quotations or author endorsements.

useWhen: Which change would be harder to understand without movement?
avoidWhen: Do not stack stagger, tilt, blur and entrance effects on the same element.
inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Give every animation a purpose” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
acceptance: Toggle twice before a transition ends: the latest state wins. With reduced motion, all information and controls remain available immediately.
Every kept animation has a written purpose.
High-frequency and keyboard paths are animation-free.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Only state or spatial continuity needs motion; repeated actions stay immediate.

comparison.bad: Every result animates in after each keystroke, delaying comparison.
comparison.good: Results update immediately; a brief emphasis on selection confirms only the changed state.
comparison.impact: Only state or spatial continuity needs motion; repeated actions stay immediate.
